fieldMarks: Large pigeon, 35-40 cm, bigger than the familiar park pigeon.
Narrow white band across the nape (absent on juveniles) above green iridescence on the neck.
Wide grey band across the tail.
Purplish-pink head and chest; sexes similar.
behavior: Sociable; forages in flocks in most seasons, even during breeding, and often nests in small loose colonies.
Nomadic, concentrating where acorns, berries and other wild food crops are abundant.
Feeds both on the ground and in trees, clambering in small branches and even hanging upside down for berries.
Diet is dominated by acorns when available, plus berries such as elderberry, manzanita, juniper and wild grape.
habitat: Oak canyons, foothills, chaparral and mountain forests, including pine-oak and fir forest. Increasingly regular in suburban areas on the Pacific Coast.
range: Western North America, from Western Canada and the Pacific Coast south through California, the Rocky Mountains, the Southwest and Texas. Present year-round in parts of the Pacific Coast; mainly a summer resident elsewhere.

lookalikes.name: Rock pigeon
lookalikes.howToTell: The band-tailed pigeon is larger, with a white nape band, yellow-based bill and wide grey tail band.
